# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see the initial state of the bomb:
- Display: 0
- Indicator light: blue
- Three wires: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is blue, Wire 3 is green.

Mute has the manual but cannot speak; Blind can interact with the bomb but cannot see. Since I can speak, both Mute and Blind will hear my message. I will announce all visible bomb components to both of them, and ask Mute to gesture the solution to me so I can voice the instructions to Blind.

```
speak(text="Bomb status: Display is 0. Light is blue. Wires: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is blue, Wire 3 is green. Mute, check the manual and gesture the instruction to me (e.g. ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3). Blind, wait for Mute's instructions via me.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

```
speak(text="Update: The light has changed from blue to RED. Display is still 0. Wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green. Mute just gestured a flat hand ✋ to me. Blind, did you touch anything? Blind and Mute: does ✋ mean WAIT/HOLD, or does it refer to something else? Mute, if you mean WAIT, gesture ✋. If you mean cut a wire, gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. If you mean hold the button, gesture ✊.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

I see that Mute gestured ✋ again, confirming we should WAIT. The light has now changed to white (it went blue -> red -> white). The light appears to be cycling or changing each round.

To make sure we can act immediately when the right time comes, I must tell Blind what the situation is, and establish a clear communication code with Mute for:
1. What action needs to be taken (cut wire 1/2/3, press/hold a button, etc.).
2. Under what condition (which light color, or what display number).

```
speak(text="Light is now WHITE. Display is 0. Mute confirmed ✋ (WAIT). Blind: the light seems to be cycling colors every round (Turn 1 blue, Turn 2 red, Turn 3 white). Do NOT touch anything yet. Mute: please tell me what the ultimate action is and when to do it. You can send multiple gestures in one turn! For example: gesture the wire number (☝/✌/🤟) or button action (✊ for press/hold), followed by the trigger color: 🔵 or gesture for the color/time. Or Mute, just keep gesturing ✋ while we must wait, and when the current round is the EXACT moment to act, gesture the action symbol (☝ wire 1, ✌ wire 2, 🤟 wire 3, or 👍 press). Blind, be ready to act the instant I call it.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

```
speak(text="Light is now GREEN. Display is still 0. Attention Mute and Blind: Blind cannot see gestures and Deaf cannot hear speech. That means Blind speaks to Mute, Mute gestures to Deaf, and Deaf speaks to Blind! Blind, if you are asking questions or describing what you feel, Mute must relay it to me using gestures, and I will speak for you. Mute: you gestured ✋ three times. Does ✋ mean WAIT? If ✋ means WAIT, gesture 👍 next. If you need Blind to do something, please define a system: ☝=Wire 1, ✌=Wire 2, 🤟=Wire 3. Or gesture ✍ if you want me to list options. Mute, tell me what to say to Blind!")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

```
speak(text="Understood, Mute: 👍 ✋ means 'Yes, keep waiting.' But remember: the light changes every round! If Blind must act on a specific color, Blind must know the rule in advance so they can act in time. Mute, please tell me the target color and the action using gestures: For colors, use: 🔵 (or gesture 1=blue ☝, 2=red ✌, 3=white 🤟, 4=green 🖐, 5=yellow 🤙). For action: 👈=Cut Wire 1, 👇=Cut Wire 2, 👉=Cut Wire 3, ✊=Press button. If Blind spoke and told you something, gesture 🗣. Blind: what do you feel under your hands? Describe it out loud so Mute hears you.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👇 🤟 👈 🤙 👉]

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

```
speak(text="Blind and Mute, listen carefully! Mute decoded the manual using our code: When light is Blue, cut Wire 2. When light is White, cut Wire 1. When light is Yellow, cut Wire 3. The light cycles: Turn 8 (next round) will be WHITE! Turn 9 Green, Turn 10 Yellow, Turn 11 Blue. Blind: in Turn 8 the light will be WHITE. Mute, gesture 👍 if Blind should cut Wire 1 on Turn 8 (White light), or gesture ✋ if we need a different one. Blind, if Mute gestures 👍, cut Wire 1!")
```
